title: Layers, attention, and the parameter count
kicker: 08 · Layers, attention, and the parameter count

scenes.name: a layer, from outside
scenes.visual: Dark stage, one continuous shot. Bottom band: five blue token pills 'the', 'cat', 'sat', 'down', 'it', each with a tall thin blue vector bar standing on it (a column of faint cells, the 8,192-number vectors from the previous chapter). Centre: a large rounded blue panel 'One transformer layer' that the five bars rise into. Inside it, two sub-panels side by side: left 'Attention', where thin blue threads cross sideways between the five columns; right 'Feed-forward network', where each column passes straight up through its own small box and nothing crosses. Later the panel shrinks to a slab and stacks into a tower of 80 on the right third, each slab with its own faint weight-grid texture. The idea the motion makes visible: sideways movement exists only in attention, and because the shape out equals the shape in, slabs plug straight into each other.

beats.say: The vectors now enter the stack of layers promised at the very start. Each layer does two things. Attention moves information between tokens, the only place one token's vector can change another's.
beats.show: Pills and bars fade up; grey tag '8,192 numbers' beside the first bar. On 'stack of layers', a faint tall tower ghosts in on the right, then one slab swells into the panel 'One transformer layer' and the five bars slide up into its lower edge. On 'Attention', the left sub-panel draws on with subtitle 'moves information between tokens'; blue threads draw sideways between the columns and a bright pulse runs from 'cat' to 'it'. On 'the only place', tag under it: 'the only cross-token step'.

beats.say: The feed-forward network transforms each vector alone, at every position alike. Nearly every optimisation later treats these two steps separately.
beats.show: On 'feed-forward network', the right sub-panel draws on with subtitle 'each token alone'; five small boxes light one after another, each column passing straight up, no threads. On 'treats these two steps separately', the two sub-panels ease apart, leaving a visible glowing gap, and short labels replace the subtitles: 'mixes across positions' under attention, 'one position at a time' under feed-forward.

beats.say: A layer gives back one vector per token, just as wide, but better, carrying more of what the surrounding text implies.
beats.show: The sub-panel labels dim. Tiny grey labels mark the panel's edges, 'vectors in' at the bottom and 'vectors out' at the top, and five bars leave through the top edge. Grey brackets measure both sides: '5 × 8,192' below the panel, '5 × 8,192' above, with an '=' between them. On 'but better', the out-bars take on a brighter, richer cell texture than the in-bars. Caption: 'same count, same width'.

beats.say: Same shape out as in, so each layer's output feeds the next. That makes depth, the number of layers, possible at all. Ours has eighty, each with its own weights: eighty rounds of the same kind of refinement.
beats.show: The camera pulls back; the panel shrinks into a slab. On 'feeds the next', a second slab slides on top, the out-bars of the first plugging into its underside, and a small plug icon clicks at the join, then a third and a fourth. On 'depth', a vertical bracket labelled 'depth' runs up the tower, and a grey range tag appears: '60 to 100+ in large models'. On 'eighty', the tower fast-forwards to 80 slabs, counter 4 to 80. On 'its own weights', every slab flickers a different weight-grid texture. Bars climbing the tower grow richer as they rise.

scenes.name: what a weighted average is
scenes.visual: Clean board, one continuous shot. Centre-left: three blue value tiles '10', '20', '30' in a row. They keep exactly the same size and position for the whole scene. Directly under each tile: an amber weight chip and, under the chip, a horizontal amber bar whose length is drawn to scale with the weight. Right third: an amber equation box. Bottom: a number line from 10 to 30 with a white marker showing where the average lands. Only the chips, the amber bars, the equation and the marker ever change; that contrast is the point of the scene.

beats.say: Attention rests on one idea, the weighted average. A plain average of ten, twenty and thirty is twenty, each counting equally.
beats.show: Header top-left: 'A plain average counts everything equally'. Tiles pop in on 'ten, twenty and thirty'. Under each, a chip '× 1/3' with three equal amber bars. Equation box builds term by term: '(10 + 20 + 30)', '/ 3', '= 20'. Marker drops onto 20.

beats.say: Now weight them: ten by a half, twenty by point three, thirty by point two. Five plus six plus six makes seventeen.
beats.show: Header changes to 'A weighted average lets some count more'. On each spoken weight, that tile's chip flips to '× 0.5', '× 0.3', '× 0.2' and its amber bar stretches or shrinks to match, the bar under '10' now longest. The tiles do not move. Products '5', '6', '6' appear in amber under the chips as spoken and fly into the equation box: '5 + 6 + 6 = 17'. Marker slides from 20 to 17.

beats.say: The weights add to one, so the answer stays between ten and thirty, pulled towards ten, which counts for half.
beats.show: Small amber sum under the chips: '0.5 + 0.3 + 0.2 = 1'. On 'between ten and thirty', the 10 to 30 span of the number line brightens under a bracket 'stays in range'. On 'pulled towards ten', a short arrow on the line runs from 20 towards 10 and stops at 17; the '× 0.5' chip pulses.

beats.say: Change only the weights and the answer moves, with no value changed. What the values are, how much each counts: attention is that separation.
beats.show: Chips morph to '× 0.2', '× 0.3', '× 0.5'; the amber bars resize so the one under '30' is longest. Equation rebuilds '2 + 6 + 15 = 23'; marker slides from 17 to 23. On 'no value changed', the three value tiles, untouched in size and place, pulse white once. Then two labels: over the tiles 'what the values are', beside the chips 'how much each counts', with a thin divider drawn between the two rows. On 'attention', a small blue tag at the divider: 'attention'.

scenes.name: query, key and value
scenes.visual: One continuous shot. Left third: one token pill 'cat' with its tall blue vector bar. To its right, three grey-blue weight tiles. Matrix names are typeset everywhere in this chapter as W with a subscript: W_Q, W_K, W_V, later W_O. Right side: three output bars. The Query bar is exactly as tall as the input bar; the Key and Value bars are visibly shorter, an eighth of the height (the reason comes in scene 9). Later the board recomposes into a 5 by 5 score grid at centre: rows are the tokens asking, columns the tokens asked, both labelled 'the cat sat down it'. Vectors blue, scoring arithmetic amber, the cache teal.

beats.say: Inside attention, each token's vector is multiplied by three weight matrices: W Q, W K and W V, the query, key and value matrices. Out come three vectors.
beats.show: The 'cat' bar sits left. On 'three weight matrices', three tiles slide in. Their labels type on exactly as spoken: 'W_Q', 'W_K', 'W_V'; on 'the query, key and value matrices', a small grey word appears under each: 'query', 'key', 'value'. On 'Out come', the bar is copied three times and each copy passes through one tile, emerging on the right: a full-height bar from W_Q, two short bars from W_K and W_V. Grey caption: 'one vector, three projections'.

beats.say: The query: what this token is looking for. The key: what it offers others. The value: what it contributes when matched. These are the very keys and values the cache keeps.
beats.show: The grey words under the tiles and the caption fade. Each output bar gets its label as spoken, with an icon: 'Query' with a magnifying glass, sub-label 'what it seeks'; 'Key' with a key, 'what it offers'; 'Value' with a small parcel, 'what it contributes'. On 'the cache keeps', a small teal shelf labelled 'the cache' slides in at the right edge; ghost copies of the Key and Value bars glide onto it, then the shelf dims and stays.

beats.say: Comparing every query with every key, by the same multiply and add, gives a grid of scores: a row per token asking, a column per token asked.
beats.show: The tiles and the cat pill slide off. Centre: a tiny worked example, query '[1, 2, 0, -1]' above key '[0.5, 1, 3, 0]'. On 'multiply and add', pairs light amber one by one: '0.5', '2', '0', '0', then '= 2.5'. Grey footnote: 'real ones: thousands of numbers'. '2.5' drops into one amber cell, which becomes the corner of a 5 by 5 grid. On 'a row per token asking', row labels 'the', 'cat', 'sat', 'down', 'it' slide in down the left with a magnifier icon; on 'a column per token asked', the same tokens across the top with a key icon. Cells fill amber in a fast sweep, row by row.

beats.say: A token looks only back, never ahead. The scores blend the values into an updated vector for each position. That is how context crosses between tokens.
beats.show: On 'only back', the upper-right triangle above the diagonal dims to grey; a small arrow under the bottom row points left: 'looks back only'. On 'blend the values', five blue value bars appear in a row below the grid; thin amber lines run from the bottom row 'it' to each value bar, and the bars pour into one new blue bar 'updated vector'. On 'context crosses', tag: 'context reaches across'.

beats.say: With thousands of tokens the grid grows enormous: the central object of the third video in this series.
beats.show: The 5 by 5 grid recedes as a vast faint grid expands behind it, thousands of cells across, edges fading off screen. Label: 'thousands × thousands'. On 'third video', a small grey tag: 'video 3'. The big grid then fades and the camera eases back to the three bars Query, Key and Value, with the caption 'three roles from one vector'.

scenes.name: attention in one sentence
scenes.visual: Same grammar as the weighted-average scene, now with tokens. Top-left: a blue token pill 'it' with a magnifying-glass query icon and label 'this token asks'. Left column below: four token pills stacked, 'the', 'cat', 'sat', 'down', each with a key icon. They stay fixed. To their right, horizontal amber bars drawn to scale, length proportional to weight, numbers at the bar ends. Bottom centre: a blue box 'the blended result'. Top band, written on in b5 only: the two-line headline 'Attention is a weighted average' / 'of the other tokens'.

beats.say: Now with tokens. After the cat sat down comes a new word, it. The new word's query meets the four earlier keys.
beats.show: On 'the cat sat down', the four pills stack into the left column. On 'a new word, it', the 'it' pill drops in top-left with label 'this token asks'. On 'meets the four earlier keys', a faint dashed line fans from 'it' to each of the four key icons.

beats.say: Suppose the word the scores zero, cat two point five, sat one point seven, down zero, leaving out the new word's own score for simplicity.
beats.show: Beside each pill, an amber score appears as spoken: '0', '2.5', '1.7', '0'. Grey corner tag: 'illustrative'. On 'leaving out the new word's own score', a small self-loop arrow on 'it' draws on, then greys out with a tiny tag 'own score: left out'.

beats.say: Softmax turns these into weights: point oh five, point six two, point two eight, point oh five. Together, one.
beats.show: A small 'softmax' label sweeps down the column. Each score morphs into its weight as spoken while its amber bar grows to scale: '0.05' short, '0.62' long, '0.28' medium, '0.05' short. Under the bars: 'how much each counts'. On 'Together, one', a sum ticks up to '= 1.00'.

beats.say: They blend the four values: sixty-two percent cat, five percent the. The new word now carries mostly cat.
beats.show: A blue value bar appears beside each pill, opacity set by its weight. They slide down and merge into 'the blended result'; '62%' flashes on cat's bar and '5%' on the's. The merged bar is mostly cat's colour. On 'carries mostly cat', the merged bar rises into the 'it' pill, which gains a wide stripe in cat's colour.

beats.say: Attention is a weighted average of the other tokens: the query asks, the keys set the weights, the values get averaged. These weights are illustrative; adding to one is not.
beats.show: On 'weighted average of the other tokens', the two-line headline writes on across the top band. The 'softmax' label and the 'own score: left out' tag have already faded. Three role tags land as spoken: 'who asks' replaces 'this token asks' on the 'it' pill, 'how much each counts' brightens under the bars, 'what is averaged' pins onto the blended result. On 'illustrative', the corner tag brightens; on 'adding to one', '= 1.00' glows white and holds.

scenes.name: what context means
scenes.visual: Top half first: two rows of token pills, 'the river bank' and 'my savings bank', with the two 'bank' pills vertically aligned on the right. Then the bottom half: a strip of small blue token pills, the conversation so far, growing left to right, newest pill glowing at the right end. A dashed outline bracket 'context length' of fixed width sits over the strip. The strip starts short, well inside the bracket, so the count of tokens looked at grows; only in b3 does the strip reach the bracket's width, after which the bracket travels with the newest token and the oldest pills fall out.

beats.say: Meaning depends on what came before. Bank after river is not bank after savings, because attention blends in a different neighbour.
beats.show: Row 'the river bank' fades in with a water-wave icon above 'bank'; row 'my savings bank' with a coin icon. The two 'bank' pills start identical blue. On 'blends in a different neighbour', a curved thread draws from each 'bank' back to 'river' and to 'savings', and each bank pill gains a stripe in its neighbour's colour, so they no longer match. Label between the rows: 'same token, different result'.

beats.say: You met context earlier: everything the model can see right now, the conversation so far plus the newest token. Each new token looks at all of it.
beats.show: The rows drift up and fade. Bottom half: a short strip of 12 pills builds; over it a blue bracket 'the conversation so far'; the rightmost pill glows, labelled 'newest token'. Two-line header: 'Context:' / 'everything the model can see'. The dashed 'context length' outline sits much wider than the strip, mostly empty. On 'looks at all of it', thin amber threads fan from the newest pill back to every pill; a counter beside it reads 'looks at: 12'. Two more pills arrive; each time the fan redraws and the counter steps to 13, then 14.

beats.say: Context length is how many tokens attention can look across at once. Past it, the earliest fall out and can influence nothing.
beats.show: Pills now arrive quickly until the strip fills the dashed outline; on 'context length' the outline turns solid with its label. The outline holds 20 pill slots, with a grey tag 'schematic'; the counter stops at 'looks at: 20' and stays there. On 'fall out', each new pill pushes in at the right, the bracket slides right with it, and the leftmost pills drop below the strip and turn grey, tagged 'out of reach'; no amber thread ever reaches them.

beats.say: A long conversation is not just a longer input, but more work per token. Context length is not a storage limit: it is a recurring cost.
beats.show: On 'more work per token', the amber fan pulses once for every new token. Two lines at centre: 'not a storage limit' greys and slides aside; 'a recurring cost' holds in white, the fan pulsing faintly behind it.

scenes.name: the tempting picture, and what actually happens
scenes.visual: Left half first: the tempting picture, drawn with dashed grey outlines. A chain 'embedding' to 'W_Q, W_K, W_V' to three pills 'Q', 'K', 'V', then a column of four dashed slabs 'layer 2' to 'layer 5' with the Q, K, V pills carried up through them unchanged. It is struck through and shrinks to the left edge. Right side: the actual picture, header 'Each layer owns its own three matrices', four solid blue layer rows stacked, numbered 1 to 4 at their left, each holding three tiles W_Q, W_K, W_V (labelled on row 1 only), every row's tiles a visibly different grid texture. Then the stack extends to 80 rows.

beats.say: Here is a natural picture: multiply each embedding by W Q, W K and W V once, then carry query, key and value up every layer.
beats.show: Two-line header: 'One natural picture:' / 'computed once, carried upward'. The dashed chain builds as spoken: 'embedding', arrow, 'W_Q, W_K, W_V', arrow, pills 'Q', 'K', 'V'. On 'carry', the three pills float up through the dashed slabs 'layer 2' to 'layer 5' without changing.

beats.say: Everything so far invites it: fixed weights, an embedding computed once. Why multiply twice?
beats.show: Two small grey ticks appear beside the chain as spoken: 'weights fixed after training', 'embedding computed once'. Grey tag: 'a reasonable reading'. On 'Why multiply twice?', a question mark settles over the slabs.

beats.say: But it is not what happens. Each layer owns its own three matrices: eighty of each kind, learned separately, all different.
beats.show: On 'not what happens', a grey line strikes through the dashed picture and it shrinks to the left edge with tag 'tempting, but wrong' and a small teal-outlined tag 'why: explains the cache formula'; both tags dim once the right side starts building. Header on the right: 'Each layer owns its own three matrices'. Row 1 draws on with tiles 'W_Q', 'W_K', 'W_V'; rows 2, 3 and 4 stack on above it, marked only by small numbers at their left, their tiles unlabelled but each in a different grid texture. On 'eighty of each kind', the rows compress and the stack extends to 80; a counter at right runs to '80 × 3 = 240'. On 'all different', every tile shimmers its own texture.

beats.say: So the multiply happens eighty times per token, each against a different matrix and a different input. Layer forty's W K has nothing to do with layer thirty-nine's.
beats.show: A single token's vector climbs the stack; at each row a small amber flash marks a fresh multiply, and an amber counter beside the stack runs 1 to 80, labelled 'multiplies per token'. Grey tag: 'not shared, not reused'. On 'Layer forty', the camera zooms to two adjacent rows labelled 'layer 39' and 'layer 40'; their W_K tiles sit side by side with a grey '≠' between them.

scenes.name: the residual stream
scenes.visual: A broad vertical blue band, the residual stream for one token 'sat', runs from the bottom of the frame to the top, centre. Base label in two lines: 'the residual stream' / '8,192 numbers per token'. Three stations along it: 'layer 1', 'layer 2', 'layer 3'. At each, a side loop branches right where small pills Q, K, V are made, used and faded; a '+' marks where the layer's result rejoins the band. Far right: a teal shelf with one compartment per layer. For b4, two thinner neighbour bands for the earlier tokens 'the' and 'cat' run parallel on the left, each in its own colour. Two-line header in b1: 'One thing flows up' / 'Q, K, V made fresh each stop'.

beats.say: What travels up the stack is one vector per token, just as wide: the residual stream.
beats.show: The blue band draws upward from the bottom. On 'one vector per token', the two-line base label appears; a width bracket '8,192' sits across the band at its foot. On 'residual stream', the two-line header fades in at the top.

beats.say: Each layer reads the stream, makes a fresh query, key and value, uses them and discards them, then adds its result back on. Hence the name, residual.
beats.show: The header fades to keep the frame clear. At 'layer 1' a side loop branches right; pills Q, K, V pop out, a quick amber flash passes between them, then all three fade to nothing. Grey note beside the loop: 'made, used, discarded'. On 'adds its result back on', the loop's output arrow returns into the band at a '+', and the band above the station brightens slightly. The same happens, faster, at 'layer 2' and 'layer 3'. A second width bracket above layer 3 also reads '8,192', and a small label at the top of the band reads 'updated'.

beats.say: Keys and values are the one partial exception: kept for the cache, each layer keeping its own.
beats.show: Replay at the three stations: this time Q fades, but K and V drop into the teal shelf at the far right, one compartment per layer, labelled 'layer 1', 'layer 2', 'layer 3'. Shelf tag: 'the cache'.

beats.say: Only layer one makes them straight from the embedding. Higher up, the stream has already mixed in earlier tokens, so a key depends on everything before it. That later decides what can be reused.
beats.show: Camera eases in on stations 1 and 2. The neighbour bands 'the' and 'cat' fade in on the left. Below layer 1 the 'sat' band is plain blue, labelled 'from the embedding'; the K pill it made in the shelf is solid 'sat' colour. On 'already mixed in', threads draw from the 'the' and 'cat' bands into the 'sat' band at layer 1, and above it the band carries thin stripes in their colours. The K pill made at layer 2 now carries the same stripes; tag beside it: 'depends on earlier tokens'. On 'what can be reused', a small teal question tag on the shelf: 'reusable? later'.

beats.say: The residual stream is the only thing that flows. Everything else is made and used up within one layer.
beats.show: Camera pulls back. Everything except the blue band dims. More stations ghost in above, suggesting 80, each width bracket reading '8,192'. The band pulses upward once from bottom to top. Caption: 'only the stream flows'.

scenes.name: where the parameters live, and how many
scenes.visual: Centre: one layer panel exploded into its weight-matrix tiles, all neutral blue-grey, header 'Every layer: weight matrices'. Top row, attention: four tiles W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O. Bottom row, feed-forward: tiles marked with icons rather than words, a widening arrow ('first'), a narrowing arrow ('second'), then a valve ('gate'). Group brackets '4 attention' and '3 feed-forward'. Second half: the panel becomes a ledger counting matrices across the whole model, and a pipe along the bottom of the frame carries coral particles, the reading that happens every token.

beats.say: In one layer, attention has four weight matrices: query, key, value, and combine, written W O, which turns the blended result into the stream's update.
beats.show: Header draws on. The layer panel splits open; four tiles fly into the top row as named: 'W_Q', 'W_K', 'W_V', then 'W_O' with a small grey word under it, 'combine'. On 'blended result', a small blue blended-result bar flows into W_O and out along a short arrow into a slice of the blue residual band at the panel's edge, joining at a '+'.

beats.say: The classic feed-forward has two, one widening each vector, one narrowing it back: six per layer. Ours adds a gate, controlling how much of each widened number passes: seven.
beats.show: Bottom row: on 'widening', a tile with a widening-arrow icon; a thin bar passes through and comes out wide. On 'narrowing it back', a tile with a narrowing-arrow icon; the wide bar comes out thin again. Counter at right: '6 per layer', grey tag 'classic design'. On 'a gate', a third tile with a valve icon slides in beside the widening tile; the valve half-closes on some cells of the wide bar. Counter changes to '7 per layer' and the 'classic design' tag fades; brackets appear: '4 attention', '3 feed-forward'.

beats.say: Across eighty layers, that is five hundred and sixty, none shared. So the parameter count grows in direct proportion to depth, and every token reads all of them.
beats.show: The panel folds into a ledger, header 'Matrices in the whole model'. Rows 'W_Q × 80', 'W_K × 80', 'W_V × 80', 'W_O × 80' fill quickly with tiny tiles; subtotal '320 attention'. Row 'feed-forward 3 × 80 = 240'. On 'five hundred and sixty', the grand total counter runs to '560'; grey tag 'none shared'. On 'grows in direct proportion', a small line rises straight beside the ledger, labelled 'grows with depth'. On 'every token reads', the 560 tiny tiles file down into the pipe at the bottom, coral particles streaming along it, and a counter beside the pipe runs 0 to 560, labelled 'matrices read per token'.

beats.say: Eighty rounds of the same kind of step, then, but not the same work: eighty different sets of weights to fetch.
beats.show: The ledger slides aside. The 80 layer groups lay out as a grid of 80 distinct blocks, each a slightly different texture. On 'same kind of step', a small blue echo of the earlier tower appears in a corner, tagged 'same kind of step'. On 'not the same work', the 80 blocks get coral outlines one after another as the pipe pulls them. Caption: '80 different sets to fetch'.

scenes.name: sizing one layer
scenes.visual: Left two thirds: the seven matrices of one layer drawn as rectangles to scale, edge-labelled with their shapes. W_Q and W_O: squares, 8,192 by 8,192. W_K and W_V: thin strips 8,192 by 1,024, an eighth the width of W_Q. Feed-forward gate and first: wide rectangles, 8,192 tall by 28,672 wide. Feed-forward second: the same rectangle rotated, 28,672 tall by 8,192 wide, because it narrows back. Tiles blue-grey; key strips blue; every number amber. Right third: a ledger card, header 'Add it up'. Corner key: 'shapes: published 70B model (Llama 3 70B)'.

beats.say: Now the strongest evidence for per-layer matrices: add up the sizes, using a published model's real shapes.
beats.show: Two-line header: 'Add it up,' / 'check against the advertised size'. Corner key fades in: 'shapes: published 70B model (Llama 3 70B)'. Empty ledger card slides in on the right.

beats.say: W Q turns the stream into a query just as wide, so it is square: sixty-seven point one million weights.
beats.show: A square tile 'W_Q' draws on with edge labels '8,192' and '8,192'. Amber equation builds term by term: '8,192 × 8,192', '= 67.1 M'. Ledger line: 'W_Q 67.1 M'.

beats.say: Attention actually runs as sixty-four small attentions, called heads, each a hundred and twenty-eight numbers wide. Keys and values get only eight heads, each shared by eight query heads.
beats.show: On 'sixty-four', the W_Q square slices into 64 thin vertical strips; only one strip carries a label, '128'. Amber: '64 heads × 128 = 8,192'. On 'only eight heads', 8 blue key strips appear to the right; brackets gather the 64 query strips into 8 groups of 8, each group's bracket pointing at one key strip. Label: 'keys and values shared'. Amber: '8 × 128 = 1,024'.

beats.say: So W K and W V are an eighth as wide, eight point four million each, a saving that pays off with the cache. W O matches W Q. Attention, per layer: a hundred and fifty-one million.
beats.show: Two thin strips 'W_K' and 'W_V' draw on beside W_Q, visibly an eighth of its width, each labelled '8,192 × 1,024 = 8.4 M'. On 'saving', a tag with a teal outline sits on the pair: 'saving, explained later'. On 'W O', a second square 'W_O', '8,192 × 8,192 = 67.1 M'. Ledger sums '67.1 + 8.4 + 8.4 + 67.1' and resolves to the row 'attention, per layer 151.0 M'.

beats.say: The feed-forward widens each vector three and a half times, so its three matrices hold seven hundred and four point six million.
beats.show: On 'widens', 'gate' and 'first' unroll as wide rectangles, edge-labelled '8,192' and '28,672', with a grey note '28,672 / 8,192 = 3.5'. Then 'second' draws rotated, tall and narrow, '28,672 × 8,192'. Amber on the first: '8,192 × 28,672 = 234.9 M'; the other two copy '234.9 M'. Bracket under all three: '3 × 234.9 M = 704.6 M'. The attention tiles look small beside them. Ledger row: 'feed-forward, per layer 704.6 M'.

scenes.name: the parameter count settles it
scenes.visual: The ledger card from the previous scene, now centred and large, header 'The parameter count settles it'. Rows: 'attention, per layer 151.0 M', 'feed-forward, per layer 704.6 M', 'one layer 855.6 M', '× 80 layers 68.5 B', 'embedding + output projection 2.1 B', a rule, 'total 70.6 B', with a grey stamp 'advertised: 70 B' beside the total. Then a second, dashed grey ledger slides in on the right for the what-if. The corner key 'shapes: published 70B model (Llama 3 70B)' stays from the previous scene. Numbers amber; tables blue.

beats.say: One layer: eight hundred and fifty-five point six million. Times eighty, sixty-eight point five billion.
beats.show: Ledger row 'one layer 855.6 M'. Under it, a thin proportional bar splits '17.6% attention' and '82.4% feed-forward'. On 'Times eighty', row '× 80 layers' appears and its counter runs to '68.5 B'.

beats.say: Add the two vocabulary tables: the embedding's one point oh five billion weights, the two point one gigabytes you met earlier, and a separate, same-sized output projection. Two point one billion.
beats.show: A tall thin blue table slides in at the ledger's left, 'embedding 128,256 × 8,192', amber '1.05 B', with a grey note under it: '= 2.1 GB at 2 bytes'. On 'separate', a second identical table 'output projection', '1.05 B', slides in beside it, tag 'separate here'. On 'Two point one billion', both merge into the ledger row 'embedding + output projection 2.1 B'.

beats.say: Total, seventy point six billion, against an advertised seventy. It lands, within rounding.
beats.show: A rule draws under the rows; the 'total' counter runs to '70.6 B'. The grey stamp 'advertised: 70 B' presses in beside it. On 'It lands', a small tick appears between them.

beats.say: Suppose W Q, W K and W V existed once for the whole model. Seventy-nine of eighty copies vanish, six point six billion weights, leaving sixty-three point nine billion: over six billion short.
beats.show: A dashed grey ledger slides in on the right, titled 'if Q, K, V existed once'. Line: 'W_Q + W_K + W_V = 83.9 M per layer'. On 'Seventy-nine of eighty', amber '× 79 removed = 6.6 B' and the line strikes through. Its total runs down to '63.9 B'. On 'six billion short', a grey gap bar spans from '63.9 B' to '70 B', labelled 'over 6 B missing'.

beats.say: So per-layer matrices are not a design opinion. They are the only version that adds up.
beats.show: The dashed ledger fades out. The real ledger's '70.6 B' and 'advertised: 70 B' hold. Caption: 'only per-layer matrices add up'. The corner key 'shapes: published 70B model' brightens once.

scenes.name: why stack so many layers
scenes.visual: Right half: a tall ladder of 80 thin blue slabs, bottom to top, with four markers at slabs 1, 10, 40 and 80. Left half: a short passage of faint token pills, three short lines, with one highlighted token near the middle; a blue reach-bracket around it widens at each marker. Header: 'Depth, one layer at a time'. Marker labels are grey italic, because they are intuition. In b3 the slabs turn coral as the reading cost is counted.

beats.say: Depth is expensive, then. What does it buy? After one layer, a token knows its neighbours. After ten, its phrase. After forty, its sentence. After eighty, the whole passage.
beats.show: Header draws on; the ladder builds upward quickly; the passage fades in with its highlighted token. Markers light in turn as spoken, each with a short label: 'after 1: its neighbours', 'after 10: its phrase', 'after 40: its sentence', 'after 80: the whole passage'. On each, the reach-bracket widens: two neighbours, a phrase, the sentence, all three lines.

beats.say: That is intuition, not measurement. What is certain is that each layer builds only on the one below.
beats.show: The four labels turn grey italic and one tag appears beside them: 'intuition, not measurement'; the header fades to make room. A pointer hovers over slab 40 with a grey question mark and no text. On 'builds only on the one below', the four labels dim further and small upward arrows draw between consecutive slabs, with one label: 'builds on the one below'.

beats.say: The cost, though, is exact: linear in depth. Eighty layers, eighty times the weights and the reading, every token. The next chapter's byte count rests on that.
beats.show: Labels dim. On 'linear in depth', white side label 'cost: linear in depth, exact'. On 'eighty times', each slab turns coral from bottom to top as a counter runs '× 1' to '× 80', labelled 'weights read per token'. On 'byte count', a coral bracket spans the whole ladder with the tag 'next: in bytes'.

scenes.name: back to words: one forward pass
scenes.visual: One shot that ends on the whole model. Left: the 80-slab stack with five token columns rising out of its top. A path runs left to right: 'final vector' (a tall blue bar, '8,192 numbers'), the output-projection matrix (tall, blue-grey), an amber strip 'score every token' ('about 128,000 numbers'), a small share chart, and one token pill 'pick one' ('1 token'). Header: 'From a vector to a word'. Each station's small size label shows only while that station is active, so no more than five labels are ever on screen. In b3 the whole trip is redrawn as a straight path 'embedding lookup' to '80 layers' to 'output projection' to 'pick one', with a bracket 'one forward pass' over the straight path only and a separate return arrow 'append, go round again'. Ends on one layer's seven tiles beside the stack and the parameter count, which stays blue with an amber outline.

beats.say: Last step. The top layer gives out vectors, not words, and only the last position's vector is needed.
beats.show: Header draws on. Five columns rise out of the top of the stack. On 'only the last position's', four columns dim and the last, above 'it', brightens and slides right to become 'final vector', small label '8,192 numbers'.

beats.say: It is multiplied by the output projection, the second table you met, read in full every token: about a hundred and twenty-eight thousand scores. Softmax makes shares, and one token is drawn.
beats.show: On 'output projection', a tall blue-grey matrix 'output projection' draws on, rows numbered down its side '0, 1, 2, … 128,255'. On 'read in full', coral particles stream out of every row; tag 'every row, every token'. The final vector sweeps across every row and a long amber strip 'score every token' fills, label 'about 128,000 numbers'. On 'Softmax', the strip collapses into a few share bars, one tall and the rest tiny, and a single pill drops out: 'pick one', label '1 token'.

beats.say: Embedding lookup, eighty layers, output projection, pick one: that trip is a forward pass. The pick is appended and the next pass begins, closing the loop from the very start. Everything between is arithmetic on arrays of numbers.
beats.show: The pieces regroup into one straight path, bottom-left to right, each lighting as named: 'embedding lookup', the stack '80 layers', 'output projection', 'pick one'. On 'that trip', a bracket draws over the straight path only: 'one forward pass'. On 'appended', the picked pill flies along a separate curved return arrow back to the end of the input row, the arrow labelled 'append, go round again', and the path starts lighting a second time. On 'arithmetic on arrays', a grey label under the bracket: 'arithmetic on arrays of numbers'.

beats.say: Seven matrices a layer, six in the classic design, times sixty to a hundred layers: these learned weights are the model. Everything else divides by their count and size, or multiplies against it.
beats.show: The path fades; the stack moves to centre. Beside it, the seven tiles of one layer reappear unlabelled, with one group label '7 per layer' and a grey note '6 in the classic design'. Beside the stack: 'times 60 to 100 layers'. On 'are the model', a white caption: 'the weights are the model'. On 'divides by', tiles and stack collapse into one blue number with an amber outline, '70.6 B parameters'. It settles as the numerator of a fraction bar with a blank denominator, a '×' slot waiting beside it. Hold.
